subject: Architecture
title: Pantheon in Rome: Temple to All Gods
description: Learn Pantheon in Rome: Temple to All Gods in one minute.

hook.text: The Pantheon's dome is 2,000 years old and still the largest unreinforced concrete dome in the world.

buildup.text: A 27-foot hole at the top — the oculus — is the only light source. Rain falls through it onto the marble floor.

discovery.text: The dome's weight decreases toward the top — Romans used lighter volcanic pumice in the upper concrete layers.

twist.text: The interior height equals its diameter — 142 feet — making the space a perfect sphere.

climax.text: On April 21, Rome's birthday, sunlight through the oculus hits the entrance perfectly — a cosmic spotlight.

punchline.text: A hole in the ceiling became the most famous skylight in history.

quiz.question: What is the Pantheon's oculus?
options: A golden altar dedicated to Jupiter
A 27-foot opening at the top of the dome
A ring of columns supporting the entrance portico

details.summary: The Pantheon in Rome, rebuilt by Emperor Hadrian around 125 CE, features the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome at 43.3 meters in diameter. Its central oculus — a 9-meter open hole at the dome's summit — is the building's only light source.
details.whyItMatters: The Pantheon proved that sacred space could be defined by geometry and light alone, without elaborate decoration. Its perfect hemisphere, where the dome's height equals its diameter.
takeaways: World's largest unreinforced concrete dome at 43.3 meters
Central oculus creates a moving spotlight tracking the sun
A perfect hemisphere inside — the dome height equals its diameter

faq.question: What happens when it rains through the oculus?
faq.answer: Rain does fall through the 9-meter opening into the interior. The floor slopes slightly toward discreet drainage channels at the center. The amount of rain entering is limited because warm air rising through the oculus breaks up falling drops, creating a misting effect rather than heavy rainfall.

faq.question: How has the Pantheon survived nearly 2,000 years?
faq.answer: Roman concrete with volcanic ash (pozzolana) gets stronger over time. The dome's thickness decreases toward the top, reducing weight, and coffers carved into the ceiling remove concrete without weakening the structure. Continuous use as a church since 609 CE ensured regular maintenance.
